$comment: Config for tools/reader-existence.mjs, seeded 2026-09-20 — ported from the Antitube harness
(PD-14 / RCA-15 R7) and adapted to stallion's contract surfaces.
THE LAW: every member of a shared-contract string union needs BOTH a producer (code that
writes the value) and a consumer (code that branches on it) in production code. Export-level
dead-code analysis cannot see a dead member inside a USED union — the 2026-07-15 RCA lesson,
kept generalized in the tool's header.
THE KNOWN LIMIT THAT SHAPES THIS BASELINE: the tool matches LITERALS. Stallion's biggest
producers are the CLIs themselves — `new --risk-class <class>`, `record --severity <S>` pass
the member as an argv VARIABLE, invisible to literal matching. Every RISK_CLASSES and
SEVERITIES row below is that shape: consumed by real guard branches, produced only from the
terminal. Read NO_PRODUCER as "no code path hard-codes it", never "unreachable". These rows
are the recorded blind spot, not hidden by deletion — a baseline that lies in the reassuring
direction is worse than one that over-reports.
WHY PHASES (tools/task-state.mjs) IS NOT SWEPT: the plugin's agreement probe builds its
fixture matrix as an ITERATED array (const phases = [...]; for...of — agreement-check.mjs),
and an iterated array is not a predicate, so every member classifies AMBIGUOUS there; one
ambiguous use suppresses every verdict for the member. A PHASES sweep today would report
zero findings while certifying nothing — the exact vacuity that once got an Antitube baseline
row deleted in error. Phase literals also flow as argv variables (`advance <phase>`). Re-add
PHASES only with a classifier that resolves iteration, and read the SUPPRESSED line first.
WHY THE LANE SLUGS ARE NOT SWEPT: the eight adversarial escape-class lanes are headings in
docs/ADVERSARIAL-CHECKLIST.md, derived at runtime by lanesFromChecklist() into computed
slugs — there is no literal lane union in code to sweep. task-findings' `lane` field is a
positive integer, not a vocabulary.
CORPUS: roots are config; test artifacts by name, inline selfTest* function bodies, contract
declaration ranges, and the tool itself are excluded BY LAW (see the tool's header — stallion
keeps its tests inside production files, so the corpus cuts the function, not the file).
Every exclusion here carries a why; a reasonless exclusion fails the gate.
Removing an accepted row is how this file shrinks. That is the intended direction of travel:
the gate refuses a row that is no longer a finding (a baseline nobody prunes becomes a
permission slip), exactly as it refuses a finding with no row.

exclude.why: the battery sandbox factory — writes fixture trees and battery strings into sandboxes: test scaffolding, not the lifecycle's production surface. grade.mjs and tasks.mjs stay in the corpus; they are shipped tools.

accepted.RISK_CLASSES.planning-only: NO_PRODUCER — consumed by IMPLEMENTATION_FORBIDDEN (executionGuard refuses implementation for this class) and NON_CODE_CLASSES (verificationGuard waives the command-pin law); the only producer is generic: `new --risk-class planning-only` passes the string as an argv variable, which literal matching cannot see (the tool's KNOWN LIMIT). No code path hard-codes the write; the class is terminal-reachable.
accepted.RISK_CLASSES.docs-only: NO_PRODUCER — consumed by NON_CODE_CLASSES (task-state.mjs, pin-law waiver) and by recordRefusal (task-coverage.mjs: a docs-only record can never authorize code at the fence); producer is generic argv (`new --risk-class docs-only`). Same known-limit shape as planning-only.
accepted.RISK_CLASSES.runtime-code: NO_CONSUMER — produced literally by the agreement probe's synthetic record (tools/zcode-plugin/lib/agreement-check.mjs) and by the authoring gate's tier probe (tools/zcode-plugin/lib/gate-law.mjs newTaskFix: would a runtime-code task be refused scoping this path?), and by the path-obligations fence-surface probe (tools/path-obligations.mjs SELF_SERVE: would a runtime-code self-serve scope over this path refuse?); no production branch tests for it BY DESIGN: runtime-code is the default class that passes every guard, and the guards branch on the restricted sets (IMPLEMENTATION_FORBIDDEN, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, NON_CODE_CLASSES), never on the default. The real producer is argv (`--risk-class runtime-code`, named unquoted in every remedy string and AGENTS.md, which literal matching rightly ignores). The honest shape of a default member, not a gap to close. (Re-accepted 2026-09-20: the retire-law wave's case helpers briefly escaped the selfTest* corpus cut, suppressed this verdict, and pruned this row as 'stale' — an adversarial pass caught the manufactured staleness; the helpers are named selfTest* again and the row rides.)
accepted.RISK_CLASSES.protected: NO_PRODUCER — consumed by APPROVAL_REQUIRED (executionGuard demands a recorded owner approval; fenceSurfaceRefusal makes fence-surface scope protected-tier blast radius); producer is generic argv (`new --risk-class protected`). Known-limit shape.
accepted.RISK_CLASSES.migration: NO_PRODUCER — consumed by APPROVAL_REQUIRED (same tier law as protected: a migration task needs an approval event before executing); producer is generic argv. Known-limit shape.
accepted.RISK_CLASSES.experiment: NO_PRODUCER — consumed by IMPLEMENTATION_FORBIDDEN and NON_CODE_CLASSES (an experiment task can never reach executing and owes no command pin); producer is generic argv. Known-limit shape.
accepted.SEVERITIES.CRITICAL: NO_PRODUCER — consumed by the proof law (task-findings shapeError and raiseSeverity: a CRITICAL/HIGH finding owes a proof), adversarial-runner's knownDefectsOf (calibration keeps CRITICAL/HIGH) and task-state's metrics highs count; the only producer is generic argv (`record --severity CRITICAL`), which literal matching cannot see (the tool's KNOWN LIMIT). Known-limit shape, same as the RISK_CLASSES rows.
accepted.SEVERITIES.HIGH: NO_PRODUCER — the same consumers as CRITICAL (the proof law, knownDefectsOf, the metrics highs count); producer is generic argv (`record --severity HIGH`). Known-limit shape.
accepted.SEVERITIES.MEDIUM: DEAD as a literal by design — produced through argv (`record --severity MEDIUM`) and consumed by position: task-findings' SEVERITY_ORDER (raiseSeverity) and retrospective's SEVERITY_RANK key it UNQUOTED, which literal matching cannot see. No per-member branch should exist.
accepted.SEVERITIES.LOW: DEAD as a literal by design — same position-consumed shape as MEDIUM (SEVERITY_ORDER / SEVERITY_RANK, unquoted keys); LOW is also the class the proof law exempts by simply not naming it. No per-member branch should exist. (History: the 2026-09-20 pruning of the CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM rows was manufactured staleness — the unquoted SEVERITY_RANK keys consume nothing this sweep can see; the verdicts had been suppressed by test helpers not named selfTest*, whose fixture literals leaked into the corpus. Since 2026-09-27 the corpus cut follows reachability, not names, and the rows ride again.)
